channel.title: Forza Horizon 6 Guide — Horizon Japan
channel.description: Forza Horizon 6 lands in a fictionalised Japan with the biggest map the series has ever built — 636 cars in the live roster today (550+ at launch). item.title: Cars — list, best picks, aftermarket, Forza Edition, treasure & barn finds
item.description: Forza Horizon 6 launches with 550+ cars [WIKI] and now sits at 636 in the live roster (Aug 13, 2026). The first group lists vehicles confirmed directly by Wikipedia (key-art cover car and the cross-title loyalty rewards). The remaining groups are drawn from community guides (IGN, GamesRadar, Reddit) and are clearly marked as community-sourced. Three further groups — Japanese icons, hypercars & track toys, and muscle & super-saloons — are pulled straight from the official forza.net roster table (Updated 13 Aug 2026) and carry real Performance Index (PI) and class figures from that table [Official]. This is still a curated slice of the full 636, not a 640+ database — for that, see the links in the note on the cars hub.

item.title: Houses & Property — plus the interactive garage map & tracker
item.description: Two different sets of "8" in Horizon Japan — and mixing them up is the single most common error in FH6 property guides. Wikipedia confirms one headline property, The Estate, plus 8 Garages that double as fast-travel and car-display points [WIKI]. Separately, community guides enumerate 8 buyable player houses, each with a permanent perk that stays active wherever you spawn; Wikipedia does not enumerate those, so they are labelled community-sourced [RPS, TECH, FH6GUIDE]. The Estate (Yashiki House) is the headline — a fully buildable plot you shape with an upgraded EventLab toolset. Houses unlock through the seven Discover Japan stamp tiers (yellow Visitor → green Sightseer → blue Traveller → pink Pathfinder → orange Navigator → purple Adventurer → gold Master Explorer).
